chat.message: Why are we stopping here? This isn't the route.
Just need to check something quickly. Give me two minutes.
That was almost 3 minutes. Can we go now? I'm going to be late.
Yes, going now. Traffic is really bad on the normal route, I'm taking a bypass.
Just a quick drop-off for my other gig, 90 seconds max.
You're doing another gig during MY ride? And the traffic isn't even that bad — Waze shows clear roads on the direct route.
Waze doesn't know about the accident on Van Ness. The traffic delay is real, 7 minutes of the extra 10 are traffic. The stops were brief, I admit that was wrong.

dispute.driver_statement: I took a bypass because of an accident on Van Ness that Waze didn't show yet. 7 of the 10 extra minutes were genuine traffic delay — that's 70% of the deviation. I did make two brief stops, I admit that was wrong and I shouldn't have. The first was 150 seconds, the second 90. But the route deviation itself was mostly justified by traffic. The stops were a mistake but they contributed maybe 4 minutes, not the full deviation. I've done 3400 trips, this is my first complaint about stops.
dispute.rider_statement: The driver deviated 19% from the optimal route, made TWO unscheduled stops (150 seconds and 90 seconds) to do another gig, and took a longer route claiming traffic. The traffic data shows 7 of 10 extra minutes were traffic-related, but the driver also admitted making personal stops during my ride. The 150-second stop violates the 120-second threshold in POL-4.7. The deviation exceeds 15% per POL-4.3. Even if traffic justifies part of the route, the stops are entirely the driver's fault.

policies.rule_text: If the actual route exceeds the optimal route by more than 15%, and the excess is not attributable to traffic or a rider-requested detour, the rider is refunded the distance-fare proportional to the unjustified deviation.
policies.title: Route Deviation - Refund Eligibility

policies.rule_text: Where the excess duration is wholly or substantially attributable to documented traffic conditions, the deviation is excused and no refund is due under Policy 4.3.
policies.title: Traffic-Attributable Deviation

policies.rule_text: A detour requested or expressly assented to by the rider is not an unjustified deviation, irrespective of the resulting distance.
policies.title: Rider-Requested Detour

policies.rule_text: A deviation of less than 5% does not engage Policy 4.3 and the claim is dismissed without hearing.
policies.title: De Minimis Deviation

policies.rule_text: An unscheduled stop exceeding 120 seconds that is not rider-requested is treated as unjustified deviation for the purposes of Policy 4.3.
policies.title: Unscheduled Stops
